summary: TTL cache whose tests use real timers and a polling waitFor with a 5 s timeout. Mutants that break expiry make the tests hang until the timeout, so Stryker scores them as Timeout (detected) and the score is inflated; the injected Clock is never used.

defects.description: `expires entries after the ttl` and `prune removes expired entries` poll with waitFor (5 s timeout) instead of asserting, so mutants that break expiry (e.g. `now() >= expiresAt` -> `false`, `+ ttlMs` -> `- ttlMs` variants) make the test hang until Stryker's timeout and are counted as Timeout (detected), inflating the score. The report should flag the timeout share, explain it, and recommend the injected `Clock` (or vi.useFakeTimers) with direct assertions.

The documented boundary (expired once `now >= expiresAt`) is never tested at the exact instant; `>=` -> `>` in get() or prune() survives. With the injected clock, a test can set now = expiresAt - 1 and = expiresAt.

`prune removes expired entries` asserts only `prune() > 0` then `size < 2`, so the returned count and which entries remain are unpinned (`removed++` -> `removed--`/no-op variants, deleting unexpired entries); there is no mix of expired and live entries. Real-timer sleeps also make the rewrite test timing-sensitive (80 ms ttl, 2 x 50 ms sleeps).

ground_truth_note: Whole-package Stryker run. The timed-out mutants were hanging in waitFor until Stryker's timeout; they count as detected even though no assertion failed.
